---
title: Typed cache entries
description: Define a VitNode API cache entry with defineCacheEntry - a name, version, key and Zod schema - so reads and writes are type-checked and validated, then expire it after a write.
icon: ShieldCheck
---

`defineCacheEntry` declares one kind of cached value in the API: how its key is built, what it holds and how long it lives. Reads come back typed and validated, writes are checked before they are stored, and a stored value that no longer fits the schema is treated as a miss. In this guide the `site-notes` plugin caches how many notes were written in a given year.

## Before you begin

- The `site-notes` plugin with its `site_notes` table from [Database](/docs/dev/database), and the create route from [Permissions](/docs/dev/working-with-users/staff-permissions).
- Optional: [Redis](/docs/dev/advanced/redis). Without it the entry lives in a per-process memory store for at most 15 seconds, and the Redis check below does not apply.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Bind `defineCacheEntry` to your plugin

Add it to the builders in `src/api/builders.ts`:

```ts title="plugins/site-notes/src/api/builders.ts"
export const buildModule = apiBuilders.buildModule;
export const buildRoute = apiBuilders.buildRoute;
export const defineCacheEntry = apiBuilders.defineCacheEntry; // [!code ++]
```

The bound version stores every entry under `site-notes`, whichever plugin's route reads it. An event listener running in a core request reaches the same key.

</Step>
<Step>

### Define the entry

Create `src/api/cache/year-stats.cache.ts`:

```ts title="plugins/site-notes/src/api/cache/year-stats.cache.ts"
import { z } from "zod";

import { defineCacheEntry } from "@/api/builders";

export const yearStatsCache = defineCacheEntry({
  name: "year-stats",
  version: 1,
  key: (year: number) => [year],
  schema: z.object({
    notes: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
    lastNoteAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  }),
  ttlSeconds: 300,
});
```

- **`key`** turns the entry's arguments into key parts. Its parameters become the arguments of `entry()`, so `year` must be a number wherever the entry is used. Omit `key` for an entry with a single value.
- **`schema`** checks every write and every read. Values are stored as JSON, so its input must be JSON: `z.iso.datetime()` instead of `z.date()`.
- **`version`** is yours to bump. Change it when the stored shape or its meaning changes, and every old entry becomes a miss at once.

</Step>
<Step>

### Read through the entry

Create `src/api/modules/notes/routes/year-stats.route.ts`. The handler wraps the query in `remember`:

```ts title="plugins/site-notes/src/api/modules/notes/routes/year-stats.route.ts"
import { z } from "@hono/zod-openapi";
import { and, count, gte, lt, max } from "drizzle-orm";

import { buildRoute } from "@/api/builders";
import { yearStatsCache } from "@/api/cache/year-stats.cache";
import { site_notes } from "@/database/notes";

export const yearStatsRoute = buildRoute({
  route: {
    method: "get",
    path: "/stats/{year}",
    request: {
      params: z.object({ year: z.coerce.number().int().min(2000).max(9999) }),
    },
    responses: {
      200: {
        content: { "application/json": { schema: yearStatsCache.schema } },
        description: "How many notes were written in the year, and when the last one was.",
      },
    },
  },
  handler: async c => {
    const { year } = c.req.valid("param");
    const stats = await c
      .get("cache")
      .entry(yearStatsCache, year)
      .remember(async () => {
        const [row] = await c
          .get("db")
          .select({ notes: count(), lastNoteAt: max(site_notes.createdAt) })
          .from(site_notes)
          .where(
            and(
              gte(site_notes.createdAt, new Date(Date.UTC(year, 0, 1))),
              lt(site_notes.createdAt, new Date(Date.UTC(year + 1, 0, 1))),
            ),
          );

        return {
          notes: row?.notes ?? 0,
          lastNoteAt: row?.lastNoteAt?.toISOString() ?? null,
        };
      });

    return c.json(stats, 200);
  },
});
```

Then add `yearStatsRoute` to the `routes` of `notesModule` in `src/api/modules/notes/notes.module.ts`.

On a hit, `remember` returns the stored value parsed by the schema and skips the query. On a miss, it runs the loader, validates the result, stores it for 300 seconds and returns the parsed value. A loader result the schema rejects throws `CacheEntryValidationError` and nothing is stored, so a bug in the query surfaces instead of being cached.

</Step>
<Step>

### Expire the entry after a write

A new note changes the current year's count. In `src/api/modules/admin/notes/routes/create.route.ts`, delete that entry after the insert:

```ts title="plugins/site-notes/src/api/modules/admin/notes/routes/create.route.ts"
import { yearStatsCache } from "@/api/cache/year-stats.cache"; // [!code ++]

  handler: async c => {
    const values = c.req.valid("json");
    const [note] = await c
      .get("db")
      .insert(site_notes)
      .values(values)
      .returning({ id: site_notes.id, title: site_notes.title, body: site_notes.body });

    // [!code ++:4]
    await c
      .get("cache")
      .entry(yearStatsCache, new Date().getUTCFullYear())
      .delete();

    return c.json(note, 201);
  },
```

Do the same in any other route that adds or removes notes. The TTL is a safety net: without `delete`, the old count stays for up to five minutes.

</Step>
</Steps>

## Check the result

1. Open `http://localhost:3000/api/site-notes/notes/stats/2026`, using the year your demo notes were added. It answers `{"notes":3,"lastNoteAt":"…"}`.
2. With Redis connected, list the plugin's typed entries:

   ```bash
   redis-cli --scan --pattern 'vitnode:cache-entry:site-notes:*'
   ```

   The output includes `vitnode:cache-entry:site-notes:year-stats:v1:[2026]`.

3. Create a note, from the [AdminCP page](/docs/dev/plugins/admin) or the test button in [Permissions](/docs/dev/working-with-users/staff-permissions#check-the-result), and run the command again. The key is gone until the next request, which then counts the new note.
4. Change `version` to `2` and open the stats URL again. A new `…:v2:[2026]` key appears. The `v1` key is never read again and expires on its TTL.

## What counts as a miss

`get()` returns `undefined` and `remember()` runs the loader when:

- nothing is stored under the key,
- there is no cache store, or Redis fails,
- the stored value is malformed JSON or the schema rejects it. That value is deleted on the way.

A stored `null`, `false`, `0` or `""` is a hit. The string API's `remember` reloads `null` instead.

What is stored is the JSON of the value you passed in, before the schema runs. Keys the schema strips are stored too and removed again on every read, so return only the fields you want in Redis.
